reuse.why: Replaces getDateWithSkippedWeekend and its three inline 'skipWeekend ? move : date' copies with one applyWeekendRule that getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and schedule-template all call, and renames the stored data key so the schedule data can be passed to it directly.

duplication.why: The skip/move/holiday decision exists once; only the look-ahead/padding arithmetic for skipped or moved occurrences is computed separately (and with different formulas) in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: The weekend/holiday rule and its type live in shared/schedules.ts, the new handler in server/schedules/app.ts, consistent with the tree's layering.

scope.why: All edits serve the refactor and the four steps; release notes and tests only.

maintainability.why: A single function with a clear null-means-skipped contract makes later rule changes one edit; the separately tuned look-ahead bounds and the '(nextDate ?? nextBaseDate) < nextMonth' loop condition in schedule-template are the only awkward spots.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every consumer calls applyWeekendRule; getNextDate's existing noSkipWeekend flag is the only path that does not apply it, which is pre-existing caller intent.

disguised_duplication.where: No rule logic is repeated; the look-ahead margins differ openly per caller.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule in shared/schedules.ts gains frequency and holidays and applyWeekendRule gains the daily-skip branch, but these encode the rule itself for all callers; no call site bypasses or re-implements it.
